themes_detail.label: Sewer System Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints exploded to 11 THIS WEEK—780% above the 1.2 weekly average—signaling a possible infrastructure failure or blockage affecting multiple properties in Hunts Point.
evidence: 11 sewer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (780% spike, z-score 10.07)
Spike is statistically significant and emerged with no prior warning signal
Affects basic sanitation and health—residents likely unable to flush toilets or use plumbing
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: which blocks/buildings are affected and when did residents first report problems?
Interview DEP: is there a known blockage, pipe break, or maintenance shutdown in progress? What's the ETA for repairs?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints surged to 21 LAST WEEK—784% above the 2.4 weekly average—suggesting a new venue, construction, or industrial activity generating sustained disturbance.
evidence: 21 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (784% spike, z-score 16.76)
Spike is recent and sharp—highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Concentrated in a single week suggests localized source rather than borough-wide trend
reporting_angles: Map the complaints: which avenue or intersection is generating the bulk of reports?
FOIL complaint details to identify the source—is it a new bar, nightclub, construction site, or industrial operation?

themes_detail.label: Street-Level Noise & Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Street/sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 32 LAST WEEK—783% above the 3.6 weekly average—pointing to public gatherings, street vending, or ongoing construction activity.
evidence: 32 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (783% spike, z-score 14.68)
Second-highest z-score in dataset—clear statistical outlier
Combined with commercial noise spike suggests district-wide quality-of-life deterioration
reporting_angles: Visit the blocks with highest complaints: are there new street markets, performers, or gatherings?
Talk to residents: are they losing sleep? Interview NYPD/CCRB on noise enforcement response.

themes_detail.label: Encampment Emergence
themes_detail.summary: Unsheltered encampment complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO—2300% above the 0.1 weekly average—indicating rapid homelessness growth that aligns with Community Board's repeated requests for expanded street outreach.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Community Board has repeatedly requested expanded street outreach from Department of Homeless Services—unmet need
Suggests systemic undersupply of shelter beds or outreach capacity in this district
reporting_angles: Investigate: where are the encampments? How many people? How long have they been there?
Examine the gap between Community Board requests and city resource allocation—why has street outreach not been expanded despite repeated asks?

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs jumped to 3 THIS WEEK and traffic signal complaints hit 19 THREE WEEKS AGO—both extraordinary spikes (700% and 311% respectively)—indicating neglected public infrastructure.
evidence: Street sign complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 3.77)
Traffic signal complaints: 19 THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 4.6 weekly average (311% spike, z-score 4.67)
Community Board has requested additional building inspectors and infrastructure upgrades—suggests systemic maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Visual audit: walk major intersections and document broken signals and missing/damaged signs
Request DOT data: maintenance schedules and repair backlogs for this district
